h: Making a day of it on Oxford Road
p: The building is a treat in its own right. Manchester Museum's older wings were designed by Alfred Waterhouse, the architect behind Manchester Town Hall and the Natural History Museum in London, so expect Gothic arches, stone staircases and plenty of character. The museum reopened in 2023 after a major transformation, adding new galleries and a much bigger, brighter entrance and exhibition space.

How long should you give it? Two to three hours is a good stretch for most families, and you can always break it up with a stop in the café. Because entry is free, there's no pressure to see everything in one go. Lots of locals treat it as a regular rainy-day haunt, ticking off a gallery or two each time.

A few tips: pick up a map at the start and let the kids choose one thing they're desperate to see, then build the visit around it. Some temporary exhibitions and events may need booking, so check what's on before you set off, especially in school holidays.

Oxford Road is well served by buses and Oxford Road station is a short ride or walk away, so you won't need the car. Afterwards, keep heading south and you'll reach the Whitworth, the university's art gallery, set in its own park. Carry on a little further down Wilmslow Road and you hit Rusholme's famous Curry Mile, which makes the perfect end to a museum day. Head back towards the centre instead and you're close to St Peter's Square, the Central Library and the rest of the city.
